slides.title: Things every coach has done to *keep up* with their DMs
slides.sub: Be honest, which number is you?

slides.title: Here's the list, no judgment
items: I DM'd 40 people by hand after a good post, and felt a little insane about it.
I paid a friend $50 a month to answer my DMs.
I sent voice notes so I'd sound more human.
I kept a notes app full of replies to copy and paste.
I answered "how much?" from the couch at 11:47 pm.
I followed up once, then felt too desperate to do it again.

slides.title: DM replies (do not delete)
items: Price: only send it if they ask twice
hey! did you still want me to send that over?
So sorry for the late reply!!
Voice note: say their name first
If they say "I'll think about it", check in Thursday
Never send 3 messages in a row (again)

slides.title: None of this is a *character flaw*.
slides.body: It's what happens when a post works and one person has to answer everyone. The leads are real, and so is your bedtime.

slides.title: Which number are you? Tell me in the comments, no judgment here.
slides.body: ManySetter is an AI setter for Manychat. Your first message still goes out from Manychat, then the setter takes over when the lead replies: it waits until they finish typing, asks one question at a time, and only sends your calendar to the right leads.
